notes: All borings drilled January 2025 with hollow-stem auger (HSA) rig; 3-inch OD split-spoon and Shelby tube sampling

title: Lining Panel Condition Summary
description: Summary of 200 concrete lining panel condition ratings from the September 2023 condition assessment of Reach 7.
notes: Total panels assessed: 200 (full Reach 7, Sta. 142+00 to 166+00)
Panel size: nominally 12 ft wide × 10 ft long; some variation due to field adjustments
Failed panels concentrated in Sta. 149+00 to 158+00 (highest clay swell zone) and Sta. 144+00 to 146+00 (highest ASR incidence)
ASR severity ratings: Level 1 = gel deposits without cracking; Level 2 = map cracking with gel; Level 3 = extensive map cracking, gel exudate, measurable expansion
30% of all panels show some degree of ASR (Level 1–3)

rows: No significant cracking, uniform surface, no delamination, joints intact
Minor to moderate cracking (<1/8-in width), localized scaling, minor edge delamination, minor joint seal loss
Freeze-thaw scaling; hairline shrinkage cracks; minor joint seal deterioration
Extensive cracking (1/8–1/2-in width), surface spalling, significant delamination, joint seal failed, some displacement
Freeze-thaw damage; ASR (Level 1–2); clay swell displacement; joint seal failure with seepage staining
Structural failure; panels broken into multiple fragments, severe displacement or upheaval, total loss of integrity
Clay swell heave (2–6-in uplift); severe ASR (Level 2–3); freeze-thaw delamination; loess collapse settlement

description: Inflow-outflow seepage measurements for Reach 7 (Sta. 142+00 to 166+00, 2,400 LF) conducted during the 2023 irrigation season.
notes: Flows measured with calibrated staff gauges and handheld velocity meters (Marsh-McBirney FlowMate 2000)
USBR target seepage rate for concrete-lined canal in good condition: 0.5–1.0 cfs/1,000 LF
Measured losses are 7–16× above acceptable target levels
Average loss over 5 measurements: 18.0 cfs total reach; 7.51 cfs/1,000 LF; 8.3% of flow
Annualized loss estimate: 5,400 AF/yr based on 210-day season, average 18 cfs loss, adjusted for variable flow

notes: Test section length: 600 LF (Sta. 150+00 to 156+00); test section isolated with inflatable dams
Water surface area at 5.5 ft depth: 12 ft + 2 × (1.5 × 5.5) = 28.5 ft bottom + sides = approximately 17,700 ft² wetted area

Higher than inflow-outflow measurement (7.7 cfs/1,000 LF) because test section coincides with most severely failed panels
Back-calculated effective hydraulic conductivity of existing lining: k_eff ≈ 5×10⁻⁵ cm/s
1-inch decline in water level over 600 LF × 17,700 ft² = 14,750 gallons per inch of decline

title: Loess Index Properties (Unit 1) — Laboratory Results
description: Index properties for loess (Unit 1, ML/CL) samples collected from borings BH-SC-01 through BH-SC-04, January 2025.
notes: Atterberg limits per ASTM D4318; unit weight per ASTM D7263; gradation per ASTM D7928 (hydrometer) and D6913 (sieve)
Apparent cohesion from matric suction estimated at 150–200 psf for natural (unsaturated) loess samples
All samples show characteristic loess composition: silt-dominated, low clay fraction, non-plastic to low-plasticity
Specific gravity Gs = 2.67–2.69 (mean 2.68, carbonite-bearing silts)
source: HDE Geotechnical Investigation Report — Reach 7 (March 2025); Lab Testing by Intermountain Geotechnical Laboratory

title: Lacustrine Clay Index Properties (Unit 2) — Laboratory Results
description: Index properties for lacustrine clay (Unit 2, CH) samples collected from borings BH-SC-01 through BH-SC-04, January 2025.
notes: Mineralogy confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis at three depths; montmorillonite 65–75% of clay fraction
Activity A = PI / (% clay fraction); A = 0.70–0.74 consistent with montmorillonite-dominated assemblage
Specific gravity Gs = 2.72–2.76 (mean 2.74, higher than loess due to clay minerals)
All samples classify as CH (fat clay) per USCS; 'very high' expansion potential per AASHTO M-145 criteria (PI > 35 for deepest samples)
Preconsolidation pressure σ'p from oedometer tests: 1.2–1.8 tsf (lightly to moderately overconsolidated)
source: HDE Geotechnical Investigation Report — Reach 7 (March 2025); XRD analysis by University of Idaho Soils Lab

title: Swell Pressure and Free Swell Test Results
description: One-dimensional swell pressure (ASTM D4546 Method A — constant volume) and free swell (ASTM D4546 Method C) results for lacustrine clay samples, Reach 7.
notes: ASTM D4546 Method A: Sample loaded to in-situ overburden stress + panel weight surcharge, then inundated; stress adjusted to maintain constant height; equilibrium pressure = swell pressure
ASTM D4546 Method C: Sample inundated under 144 psf (1 psi) token surcharge; free swell % = (final height - initial height) / initial height × 100
Expansion ratings: Low <0.5%, Medium 0.5–1.5%, High 1.5–5%, Very High >5% (after ASTM D4546 Appendix)
Panel self-weight ≈ 50 psf; swell pressure exceeds panel weight by factor 72–130× — fundamental design driver
Samples SC-01-14.5, SC-02-15.5, SC-03-14.0 represent deepest and most expansive clay encountered
source: HDE Geotechnical Investigation Report — Reach 7 (March 2025); ASTM D4546-14

title: Collapse Potential Test Results — Loess (Unit 1)
description: Single-oedometer collapse potential tests (ASTM D5333) on loess samples from Reach 7. Samples loaded to 4 tsf (representative of overburden + canal water + surcharge loading), then inundated.
notes_additional: BH-SC-04 sample at 5.0 ft (SC-04-5.0) shows highest collapse potential (CP = 9.17%); this area has least prior irrigation exposure and most intact metastable structure
notes: CP = Δe / (1 + e₀) × 100% after Jennings and Knight (1975)
Classification: <1% = No problem; 1–5% = Moderate; 5–10% = Moderately severe; 10–20% = Severe; >20% = Very severe
Applied stress for inundation: 4.0 tsf = 8,000 psf (represents 8 ft overburden at 90 pcf + 5.5 ft water at 62.4 pcf + construction equipment surcharge)
Collapse in loess beneath existing canal may have partially occurred (1962 to present); material directly under canal may have lower remaining CP
Differential collapse settlements of 3–8 inches across panel widths consistent with pattern of cracking and joint offset observed in existing lining
source: HDE Geotechnical Investigation Report — Reach 7 (March 2025); ASTM D5333-03

title: Direct Shear Test Results — Peak and Residual Strength Parameters
description: Consolidated-drained (CD) direct shear test results for key materials in the Reach 7 slope stability analyses. Tests conducted in 4-inch square shear box at three normal stresses.
notes: All CD direct shear tests: samples saturated under normal stress before shearing; shear rate 0.0006 in/min to ensure drainage
Residual parameters obtained by reversing shear direction 4–6 times until stable low-stress plateau reached
Slope stability design uses: loess (saturated, above failure plane) c' = 200 psf, φ' = 28°; slickensided clay contact c'r = 40 psf (lower bound), φ'r = 12° (lower bound) for conservative analysis
ASTM D3080-11 (Standard Test Method for Direct Shear Test of Soils Under Consolidated Drained Conditions)

rows: Peak strength from first shear; residual from large-displacement reversals
Lower cohesion due to higher clay content near contact
Residual from slickensided remolded surface; 4 reversal cycles
Deepest clay sample; lower residual c'r consistent with softer mineral assemblage
Highest residual cohesion and friction; likely higher illite content
Design range used in slope stability analyses; c'r = 40–80 psf, φ'r = 12–14° bracket for sensitivity

title: Slug Test Permeability Results — In-Situ Hydraulic Conductivity
description: In-situ hydraulic conductivity measured by slug tests in monitoring wells installed in borings BH-SC-02, BH-SC-03, and BH-SC-04 during the January 2025 investigation.
notes: All slug tests analyzed using Bouwer and Rice (1976) method for unconfined aquifers
K values represent horizontal hydraulic conductivity (dominant direction for flow in layered stratigraphy)
Five-order-of-magnitude range in k between clay (10⁻⁷ cm/s) and sand (10⁻³ cm/s) creates strong lateral flow in sand lenses
ASTM D4044 (slug tests); D4104 (Bouwer-Rice analysis)

rows: Multiple slug tests; Bouwer-Rice method; k within expected range for CH clay
Sand lens at 17.5–21.0 ft; k 10,000× greater than overlying clay — critical seepage pathway
Lower bound of clay permeability in reach; well-consolidated deeper clay
Transition zone between Units 2 and 3; intermediate permeability
Upper loess unit; k consistent with macropore structure; anisotropy likely kh/kv ≈ 3–5

title: Slope Stability Analysis Results — Spencer's Method
description: Summary of slope stability factors of safety for five analysis cases for the Reach 7 right bank slope, using Spencer's method of slices (SLOPE/W).
notes: All analyses in terms of effective stress; pore pressures from SEEP/W steady-state model
Spencer's method satisfies both force and moment equilibrium; appropriate for non-circular (translational) failure surfaces
Design criterion: FS ≥ 1.30 for sustained (irrigation season) loading with residual strength at existing failure surface
Sensitivity to drain performance: FS decreases from 1.35 to 1.18 if drainage blanket becomes fully clogged (worst case) — monitoring required
Phreatic surface for mid-season condition from calibrated SEEP/W model with existing cracked lining; phreatic surface with new lining is lower, providing additional FS margin not credited in design
source: HDE Geotechnical Investigation Report — Reach 7 (March 2025); GeoStudio SLOPE/W version 2021

rows: Dry (no irrigation; phreatic surface below failure plane)
Peak strength (c' = 200 psf, φ' = 28°) for loess; peak clay contact (c' = 300 psf, φ' = 24°)
Stable — baseline pre-irrigation condition; historically stable when dry
Mid-season irrigation phreatic surface (from SEEP/W); water table at 6 ft below bank top
Marginally stable — seepage significantly reduces FS; first-time failure risk during wet years
Residual strength at clay contact (c'r = 40 psf, φ'r = 12°); peak strength above contact
ACTIVE FAILURE — FS < 1.0 confirms ongoing slope movement; consistent with observed 2–3 ft scarp and 18-in lateral bulge
Case 4 — Remediated, Peak Strength with Drainage
Mid-season phreatic surface with drainage blanket (water table > 3 ft below slope surface)
Stable — meets FS ≥ 1.30 design criterion; adequate safety margin for peak-strength condition
Case 5 — Remediated, Residual Strength with Drainage
Mid-season phreatic surface with drainage blanket
Residual strength at clay contact (c'r = 40 psf, φ'r = 12°); controls design
Stable — meets FS ≥ 1.30 design criterion even with residual strength; drain blanket essential for achieving this FS

title: Lining Alternatives Comparison
description: Quantitative comparison of four rehabilitation alternatives for Reach 7 lining, evaluated on seepage reduction, swell resistance, service life, cost, and 40-year NPV.
notes: NPV calculated at 3.5% discount rate over 40 years (USBR project evaluation period)
All alternatives include right bank slope stabilization at $95,000 (same for all alternatives)
WaterSMART 50% cost-share applies to Alt. A: district net cost $510,000; payback 1.9 years
Alt. A service life of 40+ years is conservative; modern concrete canal linings with air entrainment, SCM, and non-reactive aggregate routinely achieve 50–60-year service lives
Annual benefit calculated at $50/AF water value; water value sensitivity: at $75/AF, Alt. A payback = 2.5 years; at $30/AF, payback = 6.3 years
source: HDE Canal Lining Design Alternatives Memo (April 2025)

rows: 6% CaO lime-stabilized subgrade (8-in depth) + 4-in sand cushion + 40-mil HDPE geomembrane + 4-in reinforced PCC (4,000 psi, 6% air, SCM, non-reactive agg., WWF, PVC waterstop at 12-ft joints)
Excellent — clay swell eliminated by lime treatment; geomembrane prevents moisture change; no heave mechanism
RECOMMENDED — Best NPV; eliminates root causes; qualifies for WaterSMART cost-share
Remove existing lining; regrade subgrade; 4-in reinforced PCC (4,000 psi, 6% air, SCM, non-reactive agg.) without geomembrane or lime treatment
Poor — clay swell not addressed; new panels will heave within 5–15 years as moisture infiltrates cracks
NOT RECOMMENDED — Short service life; clay swell will repeat failure cycle; lower NPV despite lower initial cost
Crack repair and preparation of existing panels; 2-in shotcrete overlay with fiber reinforcement applied over existing lining
Very Poor — existing clay swell continues; overlay will fail with substrate movement within 3–7 years
NOT RECOMMENDED — Negative NPV; does not address root cause; short life; highest long-term cost
Alt. D — Geomembrane Only (No New PCC)
Remove existing lining; lime-stabilized subgrade + sand cushion + 40-mil HDPE geomembrane exposed (no concrete cover)
Good — geomembrane prevents moisture changes; clay swell not chemically treated but moisture controlled
20–25 (UV degradation of exposed membrane limits life)
NOT RECOMMENDED — Lower service life than Alt. A; membrane susceptible to UV, vandalism, and debris; annual inspection and patching required
